summary: Affinity lease extension during edge retries causes routed fallback to legacy quantized variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer VeloxProducts observed a subset of traffic pinned to a new canary variant unexpectedly receiving responses from an older quantized variant after a canary eviction window. Initial hypothesis points to an affinity lease renewal that extended beyond the intended pin expiration during a burst of client retries at the edge.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests from Velox's dedicated tenant were served by a legacy quantized model for ~45 minutes.
- Some generated outputs had tokenization differences and degraded quality (customer-visible).
- No increased 5xxs reported, but customer reported quality regression and unexpected model outputs.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for VeloxProducts (tenant id vx-prod-9).
- Regions affected: us-west-2 primary, spillover into eu-central-1 via cross-region routing.
- Models involved: redwood-v2.1-large (canary), rwkv-3b-quantized-pt1 (legacy fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Velox traffic hits edge-proxy which applies session affinity tokens.
2) During a client-side retry storm (client retries on 429/timeout), the edge retries include an "x-session-anchor" header.
3) lease_renewal_handler in routing-controller recorded a lease refresh and extended the session affinity TTL past the canary pin expiry window.
4) When canary cohort evicted by scheduler, routing-controller consults session state and sees active lease -> routes to last-known compatible variant (legacy quantized).

Observed behavior:
- Affinity lease extension allowed session-state to outlive canary commitment, producing mixed routing.
- Affected requests returned outputs with tokenization/format deltas (rwkv quantization artifacts).

Expected behavior:
- lease_renewal_handler should not extend affinity TTL beyond pin_expiry boundary; after pin expiry routing should treat session as unpinned and follow rollout policy (new variant or fallback priority).

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support executed tenant-affinity-invalidate for vx-prod-9 to clear stale session anchors (admin API).
- Disabled edge retry header propagation for the tenant for 30m (edge config flag) to stop lease extensions during retries.

Next steps and owner actions:
- SRE/Serving: investigate lease_renewal_handler logic and add guard to prevent renewals beyond pin_expiry (Priya Nair).
- Serving Runtime: validate compatibility matrix to avoid routing legacy quantized model as first fallback for pinned canaries (Mateo Ruiz).
- Support: notify customer and provide list of affected time windows and workaround steps already taken (Jordan Kim).
- Schedule a hotfix backport and patch rollout to prod clusters with canary protections.

investigation_notes: Logs: edge-proxy logs show repeated requests with x-session-anchor and x-edge-retry-count. routing-controller audit shows lease renewal entries with renewed_until value extending beyond pin_expiry. Metrics: session_affinity_active_count for vx-prod-9 spiked concurrently with client retry burst. Repro steps validated in staging by replaying retry pattern against a pinned canary cohort. Root cause: renew_on_retry path lacks pin_expiry guard and routing fallback tie-breaker defaults to older model on compatibility tie.
resolution: Hotfix scheduled and PR opened (see related_github_prs). Short-term: tenant-affinity-invalidate and disabling retry header propagation executed for customer. Long-term: patch to prevent lease renewals beyond pin expiry and routing tie-breaker changes will be rolled out to all prod clusters. Postmortem to be filed after rollout targeting 2026-03-16. Follow-up actions: telemetry alert for lease_renewal_past_pin boundary and unit tests for renew_on_retry behavior.
